channel.title: AD Biomarker Field Brief
channel.description: A curated evidence monitor for Alzheimer disease biomarkers, clinical guidelines, and management updates that may change scientific exchange, diagnosis, treatment, care, or access.

item.title: Ketogenic diet trial posts inconclusive 12-week cognitive results
item.description: Registry results showed small, imprecise within-group ADAS-Cog changes and more nonserious adverse events with the ketogenic diet; no between-group effect estimate was reported.

item.title: Cannabinoid meta-analysis finds no behavioral or cognitive benefit in dementia
item.description: Nine small randomized trials did not show improved agitation, neuropsychiatric symptoms or cognition, while somnolence was more frequent with cannabinoids.

item.title: WHO updates dementia risk-reduction guidance for adults without dementia
item.description: The second edition expands prevention guidance, including environmental exposure and tailored multidomain interventions.

item.title: CELIA misses its primary dose-response endpoint despite encouraging secondary signals
item.description: Sponsor-reported phase 2 findings support further study of diranersen; they do not establish treatment benefit.

item.title: Lecanemab labeling adds subcutaneous treatment initiation
item.description: The July label permits weekly subcutaneous initiation, extending home-injection options beyond maintenance treatment.

item.title: Ceperognastat fails its clinical endpoint; higher dose worsens progression
item.description: The OGA-inhibitor trial found biomarker changes without clinical benefit, with worse outcomes at the higher dose.

item.title: FDA approves Auvelity for agitation associated with AD dementia
item.description: The April indication expansion adds a non-antipsychotic option for AD-related agitation; it is not an as-needed treatment.

item.title: ARIA workgroup updates treatment-safety and emergency-care recommendations
item.description: The Alzheimer’s Association workgroup emphasizes eligibility, MRI assessment and coordination with stroke teams during anti-amyloid treatment.

item.title: Primary-care dementia screening did not improve family quality of life in COADS
item.description: Screening neither improved family quality of life nor increased measured psychological harm over two years.

item.title: Cochrane synthesis highlights small pooled benefits and increased ARIA, with applicability disputed
item.description: The class-level synthesis informs benefit–harm discussions, but cannot substitute for drug-specific evidence.

item.title: EVOKE trials find no clinical benefit from oral semaglutide in early AD
item.description: Two phase 3 trials did not show slower clinical progression despite biomarker changes.

item.title: FDA cleared the PrecivityAD2 mass-spectrometry blood test
item.description: The cleared test combines Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau217/np-tau217 into an Amyloid Probability Score 2 for symptomatic adults aged 40 or older; current LDT availability and rollout of the cleared IVD remain distinct.

item.title: FDA cleared Elecsys pTau217 Plasma with fixed negative, intermediate, and positive cutoffs
item.description: In 958 valid participants aged 55 or older, the automated assay produced PPV 88.5%, NPV 95.3%, and 19.9% intermediate results against amyloid PET, with lower positive predictive value in primary care.

item.title: A prospective memory-clinic study found modest diagnostic changes but higher confidence after BBM disclosure
item.description: In 450 specialty-clinic patients, a p-tau181/GFAP/NfL panel changed the suspected etiology in 5% and raised median diagnostic confidence from 80% to 90%; intermediate results were common.

item.title: FDA approved Tauklarify as a second tau PET tracer for cognitively impaired adults
item.description: Florquinitau F 18 (formerly MK-6240) is now approved to identify tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology in adults with cognitive impairment being evaluated for AD, with label cautions against standalone exclusion or confirmation.

item.title: Pooled cohorts linked very high p-tau217 to 38% five-year progression risk in unimpaired adults
item.description: Among 2,684 selected cognitively unimpaired participants, very high p-tau217 was associated with 38% five-year absolute risk of cognitive impairment, but the authors cautioned against individual prognosis in unselected populations.

item.title: A 49,227-person meta-analysis defined an 11–26 Centiloid caution zone for amyloid PET
item.description: Across 53 studies, values below 11 Centiloids were high-confidence negative and values above 26 high-confidence positive in a data-driven model; the 11–26 range warrants contextual interpretation rather than an automatic binary call.

item.title: Anthem revised LAB.00046 to make qualifying blood biomarker testing medically necessary
item.description: The July policy established criteria-based medical necessity for symptomatic adults aged 50 or older using an FDA-cleared test or p-tau217/%p-tau217, while excluding asymptomatic screening and repeat testing without a new indication.

item.title: HEAD showed tau PET tracer choice changes how often tau pathology is detected
item.description: In 682 paired scans, [18F]MK-6240 detected neocortical tau more often and discriminated AD-related impairment better than flortaucipir, a valid head-to-head result that later informed the Tauklarify landscape.

item.title: eMTBR-tau243 added symptomatic-disease information after a positive %p-tau217 result
item.description: Among symptomatic %p-tau217-positive patients, adding plasma eMTBR-tau243 raised the PPV for established AD from 57% to 84% and identified high tau-PET load with 90% NPV, with similar findings in an external cohort.

item.title: Three p-tau217 platforms were compared head-to-head against amyloid and tau PET
item.description: In 113 Japanese participants, all three assays classified amyloid status well, while assay-specific analytical and diagnostic patterns differed; the small, enriched cohort and derived cutoffs limit platform-wide conclusions.

item.title: ADAPT stage 1 externally tested dual p-tau217 cutoffs against amyloid PET
item.description: Cutoffs derived against CSF in 257 participants retained roughly 90% definite-result accuracy in a small 76-person PET cohort, but the indeterminate proportion rose to 34% for Lumipulse.

item.title: Longitudinal %p-tau217 models estimated symptom onset within a 3–4 year median error
item.description: Research-cohort models linked the estimated age of plasma %p-tau217 positivity to later symptom onset, but they are not validated for individual clinical prognosis or asymptomatic screening.

item.title: FDA classified a recall of four Lumipulse plasma p-tau217 cartridge lots after falsely elevated results
item.description: Affected lots could shift results toward indeterminate or positive classifications and reduce specificity, prompting discontinuation, result review, and clinician notification.

item.title: Quanterix announced an FDA 510(k) submission for the five-analyte LucentAD Complete test
item.description: Quanterix reported submitting a Simoa-based p-tau217, Aβ42, Aβ40, GFAP, and NfL algorithm to FDA; this was a submission announcement, not a clearance or an independent validation report.

item.title: Lumipulse plasma p-tau217/Aβ42 ratio reduced indeterminate results in a specialty cohort
item.description: In 208 symptomatic specialty-care patients, the automated p-tau217/Aβ42 ratio had an AUC of 0.932 against CSF or amyloid PET and produced fewer indeterminate results than p-tau217 alone, but its cutoffs were derived in the same cohort.
